FreeBayes 1.3.6 (commit 084dce52): freebayes
Licences: FreeBayes is MIT-licensed. The program also contains HTSlib (MIT/Expat), htscodecs (BSD), SeqLib
(Apache-2.0), vcflib, tabixpp, fastahack, multichoose, smithwaterman, intervaltree and SSW (MIT), TTMath (BSD),
SIMDe (MIT), zlib, and libdisorder (GPL-2.0-or-later) – because of libdisorder the program as a whole is
distributed under the GNU GPL. Their notices are in LICENSES/ (with that of filevercmp, GPL-3.0-or-later, which
is part of the source tree; its code is not compiled into the program).
Upstream source: https://github.com/freebayes/freebayes/tree/084dce52e54af5adbd1e2b0a67f3733dd8bfddc0

Compiled to WebAssembly by the genomics-wasm project (https://github.com/comparativechrono/genomics-wasm,
commit 0e5df1fb): Emscripten 3.1.64, WebAssembly SIMD, one thread. For this site it was compiled again with
-ffile-prefix-map, so that its assert messages name the source files without the build machine's folders
(workbench/freebayes-prefix-map.patch); nothing else differs. Everything needed to build it again is in
../../../licenses/: sources/ (FreeBayes with all its submodules, zlib, SIMDe) and genomics-wasm-build/.

Changes to the source (tools/freebayes/patches there): no native backtraces (execinfo); 64-bit file offsets
with the standard off_t type; TTMath's portable C++ code with 64-bit words in place of x86 assembly.
CRAM, remote files and the freebayes-parallel wrapper are not supported. The loader (freebayes.js) was
linked for the program runner of this site and records the exit status.

Checked against FreeBayes built natively from the same source (genomics-wasm's comparison, 9 of 9 cases,
with this very build; and in the workbench, on reads mapped with bwa mem): the same VCF records, apart from
QUAL values near zero – below 1e-13 they can differ by about 1e-14, because x86 and WebAssembly compute
long double with different precision (see tools/freebayes/README.md of genomics-wasm).
